result.summary: Adds a standalone GitHub Actions workflow to run Guix builds and tests for arm64 macOS, x86_64 Linux, and x86_64 Windows. It also validates codesign environments for Windows and macOS, exports Guix time-machine metadata for caching and substitute servers, and runs unit and functional tests on the resulting release binaries using native runners.
result.problem: Release binaries produced by Guix are not continuously built or tested across native target environments in CI, leaving toolchain mismatches, broken Guix packaging, and missing codesigning dependencies undetected until release time or manual build attempts.
evidence: "Currently there is limited continuous testing of our exact release binaries. This is acceptable today as we use many similar toolchain configurations in CI which has most/everything we use in Guix pretty much covered. Many PRs also see Guix builds, although few of those probably run tests against the Guix-built binaries." (PR description)
"The regular Guix builds do not evaluate the codesign manifest, so missing imports and broken signing dependencies can go unnoticed until signing." (commit 2ca425f913)
result.scope_notes: Adds a new standalone CI workflow in `.github/workflows/guix.yml` along with supporting runner setup and test execution scripts, modifying only 6 lines inside existing Guix build scripts to retain test configuration and export time-machine variables.
result.changed_since_previous: Minor updates across CI configurations and actions steps; the core structure and workflow targets remain unchanged.
result.card: Adds a standalone GitHub Actions CI workflow to build release packages via Guix for Linux, Windows, and macOS, test codesigning environments, and execute unit and functional tests on the produced binaries across native runners. Currently, Guix packaging issues and toolchain-specific regressions are only noticed when developers manually run Guix or prepare releases. The change exports time-machine metadata for reproducible caching, downloads and installs Guix with a substitute server, and executes the functional test suite against the packaged artifacts.

risk.why: Modifications are restricted to CI workflow definitions, helper test scripts, and non-consensus Guix environment variables, posing no risk to release binaries or node operation.
